title: TRADITIONAL VS ROTH IRA: 6 THINGS TO KNOW
series_label: TRADITIONAL IRA VS ROTH IRA: 6 THINGS TO KNOW

concepts.title: The One-Line Difference
concepts.body: Traditional IRA: tax deduction now, taxed in retirement. Roth IRA: no deduction now, tax-free in retirement. Same $7,500 contribution limit in 2026 ($8,600 at 50+). The trade is when you want the IRS to take its cut — today or in 30 years.

concepts.title: Traditional Deduction Income Limits
concepts.body: The traditional IRA deduction phases out if you have a workplace retirement plan. 2026 single: $81,000–$91,000 MAGI. 2026 married joint: $129,000–$149,000 MAGI. Above the top, the deduction disappears — but you can still make nondeductible contributions.

concepts.title: Roth Contribution Income Limits
concepts.body: Roth direct contributions phase out at higher incomes. 2026 single: $153,000–$168,000 MAGI. 2026 married joint: $242,000–$252,000 MAGI. Above the top, direct Roth is off — but a backdoor Roth (contribute to traditional, convert) still works.

concepts.title: RMDs: The Catch
concepts.body: Traditional IRAs force Required Minimum Distributions starting at age 73 (SECURE 2.0). You must withdraw a % each year and pay tax on it. Roth IRAs have no RMDs during the original owner's lifetime. Big difference for late-in-life tax planning.

visual_spec.callout_text: Traditional IRA: forced withdrawals starting at 73. Roth IRA: no RMDs during your lifetime. SECURE 2.0 set the 73 age threshold.

concepts.title: Which One Fits You
concepts.body: General rule: Roth when you expect higher future tax rates (young, rising income). Traditional when you expect lower future tax rates (peak earner, expecting to retire lower). If unsure, the Roth tax-free compounding usually wins over 30+ year horizons.

concepts.title: You Can Have Both
concepts.body: No rule says choose one. Many people hold a traditional IRA for the upfront deduction, a Roth IRA for tax-free growth, and use the $7,500 total IRA limit across both. Backdoor Roth lets high earners convert nondeductible traditional contributions to Roth — same $7,500 cap, but no income limit on conversion.

visual_spec.callout_text: IRA limit ($7,500 in 2026) is shared across all your IRAs. Roth conversions don't count against the limit. Backdoor Roth works above the MAGI line.

sources_footer: Sourced from IRS IR-2025-111, IRS Publication 590-A, IRS Publication 590-B (RMDs), SECURE 2.0 Act
